items.title: Milan Fashion Week 2026 calendar confirms Gucci's Demna second show for September 25
items.summary: Italian broadcaster's fashion-week preview confirms Demna's second Gucci collection shows Friday Sept 25 at 14:00, framed as one of the week's two 'editorial highlights' alongside Fendi's Chiuri. Notes Versace's absence (awaiting new director Pieter Mulier) as a sign of continued creative-director churn across Milan houses. Neutral scheduling/preview coverage, not activation copy.

items.title: Milan Fashion Week 2026 calendar released amid industry-wide revenue and export decline
items.summary: Major Italian daily previews Milan Fashion Week (Sept 22-28) and names Demna's second Gucci ready-to-wear collection one of three closely watched 'second collections' (with Fendi's Chiuri and Marni's Rogge) that will test whether new creative identities are becoming recognizable. Sober framing: the piece stresses the fashion sector is 'still in decline' with falling exports -- neutral-to-negative industry backdrop rather than Gucci-specific criticism.

items.title: Kering stock slips even as some analysts lift price targets on Gucci recovery bets
items.summary: German financial wire covers a split analyst picture on Kering shares: some houses raised targets on hopes the Gucci turnaround under Demna and Luca de Meo is gaining traction, while the stock itself slipped, underscoring that market conviction remains fragile and unresolved ahead of the Sept 25 show and Q3 results. Independent financial-press signal, not brand messaging -- critical-angle counterweight to Kering's optimistic public framing.

items.title: Puck: what happens to Kering if Gucci's turnaround under Demna fails
items.summary: Subscription business-media piece (opinion-inflected per pool policy, corroborate hard figures) probing the downside scenario for Kering if Demna's Gucci reset does not translate into sales recovery -- framed around investor patience running thin and the group's heavy structural dependence on a single brand. Explicitly skeptical counter-narrative to management's turnaround messaging.

items.title: Trustpilot reviews of gucci.com continue to skew heavily negative on service and quality
items.summary: Aggregated consumer-review platform shows sustained pattern of complaints about after-sales service, repair turnaround (multi-month waits), unexpected repair-price increases, and quality defects (hardware/soldering, stitching) on recent purchases. Genuine unfiltered consumer-opinion channel (not brand-owned); exact review dates within the platform's rolling feed could not be pinned to a single day, engagement metrics (helpful votes) not exposed in aggregate view, left null.

items.title: French review aggregator gives Gucci 1.9/5 on repeated quality and after-sales complaints
items.summary: French-language consumer-review site aggregates 13 authenticated reviews averaging 1.9/5, citing sub-par craftsmanship, unguaranteed products, cracking solder on jewelry/bracelets after normal wear, unprofessional customer service, and repair waits stretching to five months. Independent critical-angle consumer signal surfaced directly by a French-language search, included per anti-bias mandate; platform does not expose like/share counts, left null.

items.title: TikTok fashion-commentary videos keep circulating mixed-to-negative Demna-era Gucci review clips ahead of the Sept 25 show
items.summary: Fashion TikTok discovery page shows continuing volume of reaction/review clips debating Demna's Gucci direction; titles skew skeptical (one widely surfaced short calls the Fall 2026 collection a 'flop'; another asks whether Demna is 'just repeating Tom Ford'), alongside more enthusiastic reaction content. Aggregate discovery-page signal; individual video-level like/comment/share counts not accessible via public search, left null per no-fabrication rule.

items.title: Independent YouTube fashion reviewers debate whether Demna's Gucci is 'just repeating Tom Ford'
items.summary: Independent (non-brand) YouTube review video explicitly questions whether Demna's aesthetic direction for Gucci is derivative of Tom Ford's archive-era work rather than a genuinely new identity -- part of a wider cluster of critical creator commentary sitting alongside more positive reaction videos ahead of the Sept 25 show. View/like counts not visible via search snippet, left null.
